content: Diabetic retinopathy is a significant ocular complication that occurs in individuals with both type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Its development is closely associated with the duration of diabetes and the degree of glycemic control maintained by the patient. This condition is one of the leading causes of vision loss among adults aged 20 to 74 years. The risk of developing diabetic retinopathy increases in the presence of hyperglycemia (elevated blood glucose levels), hypertension (high blood pressure), nephropathy (kidney disease), and dyslipidemia (abnormal lipid levels in the blood). These factors exacerbate the damage to the retinal blood vessels, leading to progressive visual impairment. Maintaining effective glycemic control is critical in reducing both the onset and progression of diabetic retinopathy. Proper management of blood glucose levels can significantly decrease the likelihood of requiring surgical interventions and help preserve vision in affected individuals.
